identity_evidence: Executive Order 1489 (1912), signed Wednesday, February 28, 1912; text dated February 28, 1912
basis: Sets a speed limit and rule of the road for vehicles on Canal Zone roads with a fine or jail penalty; it governs only the Zone, which ceased to exist in 1979.
end_or_bound: no later than 1979-10-01 (Zone government ceased); page header also says revoked by EO 3434, 1921-04-14
operative_quote: No automobile, motor cycle, or bicycle shall be driven or operated over the roads or streets of the Canal Zone at a speed exceeding fifteen (15) miles an hour on straight roads
notes: Revocation date comes from the Wikisource header, not the order text. Footnote says the 1908 order repealed was issued by the Secretary of War.

identity_evidence: Executive Order 2926 (1918), signed July 26, 1918, amends Paragraph 20 of the Panama Canal navigation rules
basis: Amends a canal navigation rule on responsibility for handling vessels and on claims for damage; it concerns only the U.S. operation of the canal.
end_or_bound: no later than 1999-12-31 (U.S. operation of the canal ended)
operative_quote: The captain or master of a vessel in Canal waters, except while the vessel is being passed through the locks, shall be charged with the safe handling and proper navigation of the vessel

identity_evidence: Executive Order 3255 (1920), signed March 31, 1920, Establishing Maritime Quarantine Regulations for the Canal Zone and Harbors of Panama and Colon

regulates vessels and harbors of the cities of Panama and Colon in the Republic of Panama, outside the Zone

operative_quote: I hereby establish the following maritime quarantine regulations for the Canal Zone, and for the harbors of the cities of Panama and Colon, Republic of Panama.
notes: Truncated at about 12,000 of 16,076 characters. Likely would end by 1999-12-31 if the rest is clean; needs individual review of the full text.

identity_evidence: Executive Order 2428 (1916), signed July 25, 1916, quarters, fuel and electric current for Panama Canal and Panama Railroad employees on the Isthmus
basis: Grants canal and Panama Railroad employees on the Isthmus free quarters, fuel and electric current and authorizes the Governor to assign quarters; a service-conditions order for the Zone workforce under the Panama Canal Act.
end_or_bound: no later than 1999-12-31 (U.S. operation of the canal ended)

notes: Includes Panama Railroad Company employees; rests on the Panama Canal Act of 1912, not a corporate statute. Header says amended by EO 2440.

identity_evidence: Executive Order 1295 (1911), signed February 2, 1911, method of executing and recording deeds in the Canal Zone
basis: Sets how deeds to Canal Zone land are executed and recorded, creates the Zone Registrar of Property and fees; all of it is Zone law that ended when the Zone government ended. Deeds already made are accrued effects.
operative_quote: Art. 5. The Clerk of the Circuit Court of the First Judicial Circuit of the Canal
notes: File truncated after the order's Art. 19 and signature, which is the end of this order. Art. 13 gives recording priority over later purchasers; I treat that as part of the Zone recording system, not a statute-preserved personal right.

identity_evidence: Executive Order 731 (1908), signed January 9, 1908, amends Section 22 of Act No. 1 to divide the Canal Zone into three Judicial Circuits
basis: Amends the Zone's court-circuit structure by dividing the Zone into three judicial circuits; this is Zone court organization with no object after the Zone and its courts ended.
end_or_bound: no later than 1982-03-31 (Zone courts; Zone itself ceased 1979-10-01)

notes: Claimed title says 'judicial districts'; text says 'Judicial Circuits'. Same subject.

identity_evidence: Executive Order 730 (1908), signed January 9, 1908, unclaimed property held by common carriers in the Canal Zone
basis: Lets Zone common carriers sell unclaimed freight and baggage at auction and sends unclaimed proceeds to the Canal Zone Government school fund; it is Zone law that ended with the Zone government. Completed sales are accrued effects.
operative_quote: it shall be lawful for the common carrier to sell the same at public auction, at some designated point within the Canal Zone

identity_evidence: Text dated May 29, 1934, FDR; revokes part of section 4 of Executive Order No. 6166; claimed number 6728
outliers_found: general federal reorganization of disbursing functions of the War Department, Navy Department and the Panama Canal; reaches far outside the Zone
basis: The order limits a government-wide transfer of disbursing functions and covers the War and Navy Departments as well as the Panama Canal, so the Canal mention is only one part of a federal-wide order.
operative_quote: it is ordered that the above-quoted provision of section 4 of Executive Order No. 6166 of June 10, 1933, be, and it is hereby, revoked
notes: Text does not state its own number; date and subject agree with the claimed title.

identity_evidence: Text dated August 5, 1933, FDR; postpones transfer of the District Court for the Panama Canal Zone to October 4, 1933
basis: Postpones to October 4, 1933 the transfer of the Canal Zone district court to the Department of Justice; the command is a one-time deferral that ran out on its own date.
operative_quote: the effective date of the transfer to the Department of Justice of the District Court of the United States for the Panama Canal Zone is hereby postponed to October 4, 1933.
notes: Text carries no order number; match rests on date, subject and the claimed title. It acts under section 22 of EO 6166, a general order, but its own command concerns only the Zone court.

operative_quote: Let student interpreters be included under paragraph 2 sub-division (a) and under paragraph 11, on the same footing as vice consuls, deputy consuls and consular agents.
notes: Identity matches the claimed number and date, but the order does not belong to the Canal Zone lot.

identity_evidence: Executive Order 274 (1904), signed November 15, 1904, applies civil-service rules to the Isthmian Canal Commission
